observations.content:
Summary: The speed of light in vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 m/s, as defined by the International System of Units (SI). This fixed value is used to define the metre as the distance light travels in vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second. This definition was established by the General Conference on Weights and Measures in 1983, making the speed of light a defined constant in the SI system of units.

observations.content:
Summary: The speed of light in vacuum, c, is defined to be exactly 299 792 458 m/s. This definition is established by the International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM) and is reflected in the SI Brochure, which states that the metre is defined as the distance light travels in vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second. This definition is also confirmed by Wikipedia and other sources, which emphasize that this value is exact due to international agreement and the redefinition of the metre in 1983.

### Relativity [...] ### Relativity

The speed of light in vacuum is constant, regardless of the motion of the source or the inertial reference frame of the observer.

### Speed

The speed of light in vacuum, c, forms the basis for the definition of the unit of speed, the metre per second.

The fixed numerical value of the speed of light in vacuum, c, is defined exactly:

c \mspace{4mu} = 299 \mspace{4mu} 792 \mspace{4mu} 458 \ \text{m} \ \text{s}^{-1} [...] Inverting this relation gives an exact expression for the metre per second in terms of the speed of light in vacuum, c :

1 \mspace{4mu} \text{m} \mspace{4mu} \text{s}^{-1} \mspace{4mu} = \dfrac{1}{299 \mspace{4mu} 792 \mspace{4mu} 458} \mspace{4mu} c\\  

### Length or distance

The speed of light in vacuum, c, together with the hyperfine transition frequency of the caesium 133 atom, ΔνCs, forms the basis for the definition of the unit of length, the metre.

observations.content:
Summary: The sources confirm that the speed of light in vacuum is defined as exactly 299 792 458 m/s by NIST/CODATA 2022. This exact value is used to define the metre, where one meter is the distance light travels in vacuum in 1/299792458 of a second. This definition is exact by international agreement and forms part of the International System of Units (SI).
